title: Trump: Mogilevich takes control of Inkombank, the Bank of New York's #1 partner
description_short: Trump: Mogilevich takes control of Inkombank, the Bank of New York's #1 partner
description_medium: TrumpFile's 1994 timeline entry says court documents show Semion Mogilevich reached a deal with Inkombank chairman Vladimir Vinogradov for control of the Russian bank. The page says Inkombank later became the Bank of New York's largest and most active commercial relationship; a 2008 Guardian report also describes Mogilevich's 1994 control of the bank. Neither supplied source identifies a Trump connection, and the referenced court documents are not included.

title: Trump: Journalist warns organized crime infiltrating U.S., Israel, and Europe threatens democracy
description_short: Trump: Journalist warns organized crime infiltrating U.S., Israel, and Europe threatens democracy
description_medium: TrumpFile's May 1, 2000 entry says journalist Robert I. Friedman argued in his book Red Mafiya that globalized organized crime was infiltrating businesses and governments in Israel, the United States, and Europe and threatened democracy. The page explicitly says the exact quotation and more detail would be added after the book arrived. The linked New York Times article reports on money laundering in Israel and the Bank of New York case, but does not supply Friedman's passage or a Trump connection.
description_long: In Red Mafiya, his 2000 investigation of Russian organized crime, journalist Robert I. Friedman warned that criminal networks were expanding their reach across business and government in the United States, Israel and Europe. He argued that this transnational influence could threaten democratic institutions. Friedman had spent years reporting on Russian organized crime, and the book became a major account of its growth and connections. His warning addressed how illicit networks might exploit legitimate commerce and political relationships; it was not a claim that every institution in the regions named had been captured. The work belongs to the broader history of reporting on post-Soviet criminal organizations and their international activity. Friedman died in 2002. The event is the publication and argument of his book, which framed organized crime as a political as well as law-enforcement concern. Specific present-day cases or government links require their own evidence and are not established by the book’s general warning.
notes: The readable TrumpFile page, dated May 1, 2000, attributes the warning to Friedman's 2000 book Red Mafiya and describes the countries and institutions at issue; it explicitly says the exact quote and more information were pending the book's arrival. The linked New York Times archive article (February 21, 2000) reports on Israeli money-laundering laws, officials' concerns, and investigations connected to the Bank of New York, but it does not identify Friedman's book or quote him. A checkable passage from the book and the intended connection to Trump remain missing.

title: Donald Trump signs a contract with Russia, makes hundreds of millions
description_short: Donald Trump signs a contract with Russia, makes hundreds of millions
description_medium: The readable TrumpFile entry says Donald Trump attended the Moscow Millionaire Fair in 2007 after asking Sergei Millian to help arrange the trip. It attributes a later claim to Millian that they signed Russian real-estate contracts, but says no Russian project was built; Millian's “hundreds of millions” remark refers to Russian buyers at Trump's U.S. properties. The page provides no agreement, contract terms, or records supporting the earnings figure.
description_long: Donald Trump attended the Moscow Millionaire Fair in November 2007 after asking Sergei Millian to help organize his trip to Russia. Millian was president of the Russian-American Chamber of Commerce. In April 2016, he told the Russian news agency RIA Novosti that he and Trump had signed a contract to develop real-estate projects. The reported statement came years after the fair and does not, by itself, establish when the contract was signed or what it covered. The supplied account includes no copy of the agreement, identifies no specific projects or locations, and gives no evidence that any project was completed. It also does not show how the title’s claim of “hundreds of millions” was calculated or whether that amount refers to revenue, investment, or another figure. The fair attendance and Millian’s later account can be described separately from the unsubstantiated financial claim. Until the contract and its results are documented, the headline’s characterization of a Russian deal producing hundreds of millions should not be treated as an established outcome.
notes: TrumpFile's November 22, 2007 entry confirms fair attendance as its account and says Millian helped arrange the trip. It later attributes to Millian a claim that they signed Russian real-estate development contracts, while explicitly stating that nothing was built in Russia; the quoted hundreds-of-millions figure is attributed to Russian purchases at Trump properties in the United States. No executed agreement, date/terms, completed project, or revenue record is linked, so the title's contract and earnings claims remain unverified.

title: ACLU Explains Project 2025's Proposed Changes to Federal Policy
description_short: ACLU Explains Project 2025's Proposed Changes to Federal Policy
description_medium: The ACLU's explainer describes Project 2025 as a proposed federal-policy agenda for reorganizing the executive branch, authored by the Heritage Foundation and former Trump administration officials. It outlines recommendations touching immigration, abortion rights, free speech, and racial justice, and says some proposals would require action by Congress or the executive branch. This is the ACLU's account of a plan and its civil-liberties concerns, not evidence that those changes were enacted or that rights were universally eliminated.
description_long: The ACLU's Project 2025 explainer, published August 14, 2024 and updated January 26, 2026, describes the initiative as a federal-policy agenda for restructuring the executive branch. It says the Heritage Foundation and former Trump administration officials produced the project, whose central “Mandate for Leadership” is a 900-page manual organized around federal agencies. The ACLU says the plan contains hundreds of policy recommendations touching immigration, abortion rights, free speech, racial justice, and other constitutional freedoms. It distinguishes measures that would need support from Congress or the executive branch from proposals it considers unconstitutional, and presents the material as a warning about what could follow a second Trump term. The page also describes the ACLU's response through advocacy, litigation, and community organizing. These are the organization's characterizations of a proposed agenda. The supplied source does not show that all recommendations were adopted, establish universal loss of constitutional protections, or document the broad completed outcome claimed by the original title.

preserved_fields.title: Human Rights Universal Elimination - Constitutional Protection Final Destruction
preserved_fields.description_short: Human Rights Universal Elimination - Constitutional Protection Final Destruction
preserved_fields.description_long: Donald Trump achieved universal elimination of human rights by systematically destroying all constitutional protections, civil liberties, equal protection guarantees, and individual freedoms while establishing authoritarian rule where human rights depended on political loyalty rather than constitutional guarantees or universal principles that had historically protected American citizens from government abuse. The comprehensive rights destruction represented Trump's completion of Project 2025's elimination of constitutional protections through systematic violation of First Amendment speech and assembly rights, Fourth Amendment privacy protections, Fifth Amendment due process guarantees, Eighth Amendment cruel punishment prohibitions, and Fourteenth Amendment equal protection principles. The universal rights elimination included ending freedom of speech through protest criminalization, privacy rights through surveillance expansion, due process through arbitrary detention, cruel punishment prohibitions through torture authorization, and equal protection through systematic discrimination that created legal hierarchy based on political loyalty rather than constitutional citizenship. Trump's rights destruction violated every constitutional protection by transforming human rights from universal guarantees into political privileges distributed based on loyalty to Trump rather than constitutional citizenship, effectively ending the concept of inalienable rights that had defined American democracy since the founding of the republic. The constitutional protection elimination created what human rights organizations called complete abandonment of universal human rights principles through systematic persecution that targeted individuals based on political beliefs, religious affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, racial background, and immigration status rather than criminal behavior or legal violations. The human rights elimination represented Project 2025's vision of society controlled by political hierarchy rather than constitutional equality, transforming America from constitutional democracy based on universal rights into authoritarian state where human dignity and fundamental freedoms depended on political loyalty rather than inherent human worth and constitutional protections.

notes: The linked ACLU explainer is readable and provides its publication/update dates, account of the Heritage/officials-authored agenda and 900-page manual, and its framing of recommendations as proposals and civil-liberties risks. The Civil Rights link returned HTTP 403. The replacement describes the ACLU's explanation rather than treating the plan's proposed changes as implemented outcomes.

title: Complete Union Elimination and Collective Bargaining Ban - Worker Rights Final Destruction
description_short: Complete Union Elimination and Collective Bargaining Ban - Worker Rights Final Destruction
description_medium: The accessible Better in a Union Project 2025 explainer describes proposed changes affecting union organizing, including exclusive secret-ballot recognition, expanded employer anti-union tools, and possible changes to transit-worker protections. The supplied AFL-CIO link concerns a 2025 federal-worker collective-bargaining order but returned HTTP 403, and the 2024 Project 2025 PDF could not be text-extracted in this environment. The available read does not support the claim that unions or bargaining were eliminated across public and private employment.
description_long: Donald Trump achieved complete elimination of labor unions by banning collective bargaining for all federal workers while implementing Project 2025's plan to 'end public sector unions' and make private sector organizing illegal through systematic destruction of National Labor Relations Act protections and worker rights that had enabled collective action for over 90 years. The comprehensive union destruction represented Trump's implementation of corporate control over American workers by eliminating every protection for collective bargaining while enabling employers to retaliate against organizers, decertify existing unions mid-contract, and create company-controlled sham unions that served management interests rather than worker welfare. The collective bargaining ban included directing NLRB to prosecute union leaders for political advocacy while allowing employers to negotiate away overtime protections, workplace safety requirements, and fair scheduling in exchange for token benefits that reduced worker power and economic security. Trump's union elimination violated fundamental worker rights by destroying legal protections that had enabled collective action while creating 'union-free' environment where workers faced employer retaliation without legal recourse or organizational support to address workplace abuse, wage theft, and unsafe conditions. The worker rights destruction created what labor advocates called systematic return to 'Gilded Age' exploitation where employers gained complete control over working conditions while eliminating worker voice in workplace decisions, economic security, and safety protections that unions had historically provided through collective bargaining. The complete union elimination represented Project 2025's vision of labor relations controlled by corporate interests rather than worker rights, transforming employment from protected relationship with collective bargaining into 'at-will' system where workers lacked voice, representation, or legal protection against employer abuse and exploitation through systematic elimination of labor organizing and collective action.
subcategory: Worker Rights Elimination and Union Destruction

title: Navarro Backs a Kodak Drug-Manufacturing Loan and Two COVID-Supply Contracts
description_short: Navarro Backs a Kodak Drug-Manufacturing Loan and Two COVID-Supply Contracts
description_medium: TrumpFile's March 1, 2020 timeline reports three pandemic-supply commitments promoted by trade adviser Peter Navarro: a $765 million Kodak loan for generic-drug production, a $353 million Phlow contract for pharmaceutical ingredients, and a $96 million AirBoss contract for respirators and air filters. The account says Kodak had not manufactured drugs and needed an FDA waiver, Phlow was newly formed, and Navarro pressed agencies but could not approve contracts himself. It does not establish payments or delivery outcomes.
description_long: TrumpFile's March 1, 2020 timeline says Peter Navarro urged President Trump to direct resources toward drug supplies and medical equipment, then describes three commitments. It reports a $765 million loan to Eastman Kodak to produce generic drugs, noting that Kodak had not previously manufactured drugs and needed an FDA waiver; a $353 million pharmaceutical-ingredients contract with Phlow, described as a new company that had not manufactured drugs; and a separate $96 million AirBoss Defense Group contract for respirators and air filters. The account says Navarro helped draft AirBoss's proposal and pressured agencies, while lacking authority to approve the contracts himself. It quotes a March 20 message in which he urged immediate approval of the Phlow contract. The listed loan and contracts total about $1.214 billion, but that is not evidence that the amounts were disbursed or that products were delivered. The supplied page does not include the contracts, agency award records, or completion data, so this description reports its account rather than independently verifying performance.
notes: The previously inaccessible linked TrumpFile page now loads and names Kodak, Phlow, and AirBoss with their respective $765 million loan, $353 million contract, and $96 million contract, plus the reported product and Navarro-role details. The corrected title separates drug manufacturing from the respirator/filter contract. The source does not include award instruments, payment records, or delivery outcomes, so no claim about disbursement or completed production is made.
